findings.reason: The protected implementation is concise, conventional iterative depth-first search. The lonely result list, explicit stack, parent-local left/right test, and symmetric child pushes expose the entire algorithm without helper indirection or carried parent state. The local TreeNode equivalent satisfies the standalone app contract, and no material improvement warrants an inert candidate.

Every non-root tree node has exactly one parent, and the traversal visits that parent exactly once. During that unique visit, the child is appended exactly when the opposite child field is absent, which is precisely the definition of loneliness. Parents with two or zero children contribute nothing, the root is examined only as a parent and never appended, and every existing child is pushed once so no possible parent is skipped.

Each of N nodes is pushed, popped, and inspected once, giving O(N) time. The explicit traversal stack and returned lonely-value list can each contain O(N) entries, matching the declared O(N) space bound. The complexity artifact is inherited, hash-bound identity only; this accelerated review did not inspect or recalibrate it and did not claim a fresh runtime verdict.

The implementation preserves the nonempty binary-tree contract, returns node values rather than node objects, excludes only the parentless root, and accepts either left-only or right-only children. Because output order is unrestricted, the stack's right-before-left visitation after symmetric pushes is semantically valid and avoids unnecessary sorting.

The complete Approach accurately derives parent-centered classification, the explicit stack traversal, exact-once discovery, and a representative structural trace. Its O(N) time and space claims match the protected code and manifest, and its alternatives and edge cases cover recursive and breadth-first traversal, carried loneliness flags, repeated parent searches, a single root, one-child roots, two-child parents, one-sided chains, and arbitrary output order.

The protected app source and immutable native source remain unchanged at canonical SHA-256 values c1964d130bbdbbf94d74e8f7daf7c99a01d661406728183f8ad0898d68728d15 and 4ad10b5fae40f7f403e6ee1d01c09fb4c212a7df639e71adbafaa91ba184ec15. Both use the same result list, stack order, child-pair conditions, pushes, and return; their structural differences are limited to the required local TreeNode and native Solution wrapper. Verified submission 2074749655 remains untouched.

Authenticated Premium evidence confirmed the lonely-node and root definitions, arbitrary output order, all three exact examples with complete explanations, two constraints, three example diagrams, and one traversal hint. The former legacy third example was not source-native; the modular Reference now restores the actual tree and independently recreates all three diagrams as accessible Mermaid trees with every parent-child relation and lonely-node designation. It is bound to live content SHA-256 8c36b4b98115cf37e8733e491006d79b0e955740f633964aea380392736b53b6.
